svg.title: se-dev-mes Developer Skill Features, Utilities and Architecture
svg.desc: Comprehensive architecture and toolkit diagram showcasing the workflow pipeline and four core feature pillars of the se-dev-mes developer skill, including boilerplate scaffolding, C# tag engine, silent bug auditing, and the 1.11.0 eval benchmark results.
svg.text: WORKFLOW PIPELINE · FROM ENCOUNTER GOAL TO RUNNING SERVER MOD
THE MODDER TOOLKIT · 4 CORE FEATURES & UTILITIES
New-MesProfile.ps1 instantly scaffolds ready-to-run boilerplate: convoys,
combat drones, boss carriers, store grids, and dynamic zone ladders.
Converts <!-- --> to [//] comments inside <Description>, preventing Keen's
ReadElementString from throwing fatal MOD_CRITICAL_ERROR crashes.
Add-MesProfileSnippet.ps1 injects new profiles into existing SBCs
without XML formatting damage, indentation drift, or broken closing tags.
Extracted directly from MES & RivalAI source across 41 profile schemas.
Rules classified as [HARD] binary engine limits or [SOFT] heuristics.
query_mes_tags.py instantly searches tag data types, valid parent
profiles, and syntax examples without decompiling game DLLs.
check_mes_sync.py compares installed MES updates against the offline
cache, warning immediately if upstream releases introduce new tags.
Source: MES commit 37455cf · 41 profile schemas parsed
tags that cause MES to silently ignore actions without logging errors.
Flags stripped zeroes in TagParse.cs counter targets, and unchecked
CargoShipWaypoints[0] crashes that freeze server-wide NPC AI loops.
Purges stale .sbcB5 binary caches overriding XML changes, and audits
fixed weapons saved in "Auto" mode that ignore MES fire commands.
Field-tested patterns: spawning pipelines, aircraft 90° reverse-braking
control, store grid economy sales, dereliction, and server diagnostics.
se-dev-mes v1.11.0 · GV: Deserts of Kharak Server Project · Source: Modular-Encounters-Systems C# commit 37455cf · Stamped 2026-10-14
● Gray: Architectural Design Intent ■ Blue: Code-Verified C# Constraints ▲ Orange: Empirically Measured Evals
